This action supports new instrument procedures and instrument flight rule (IFR) operations.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21812","title":"Parts and Accessories Necessary for Safe Operation; Application for an Exemption From R.B. Stewart Petroleum Products, Inc., USDOT # 1290158","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21812/parts-and-accessories-necessary-for-safe-operation-application-for-an-exemption-from-rb-stewart","summary":"FMCSA requests public comment on an application from R.B. Stewart Petroleum Products, Inc., USDOT No. 1290158, (R.B. Stewart) for an exemption from the requirement that lighting devices be steady burning. The exemption would allow the company to operate commercial motor vehicles (CMVs) equipped with a module manufactured by Intellistop, Inc. (Intellistop) which pulses the rear clearance, identification, and brake lamps from low-level lighting intensity to high-level lighting intensity 4 times in 2 seconds when the brakes are applied, and then return the lights to a steady-burning state while the brakes remain engaged. FMCSA requests public comment on the applicant's request for exemption.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21794","title":"Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards; Modernization of FMVSS No. 108 To Accommodate ADS-Equipped Vehicles","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21794/federal-motor-vehicle-safety-standards-modernization-of-fmvss-no-108-to-accommodate-ads-equipped","summary":"NHTSA is proposing to amend Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 108, \"Lamps, reflective devices, and associated equipment.\" The proposed updates to the standard are intended to remove unnecessary requirements and to provide design flexibility without impact on vehicle safety. The first two proposed changes would amend the test voltage specification for integral beam type headlamps and remove requirements that apply to vertical headlamp arrangements. Further proposed changes address vehicles equipped with Automated Driving Systems (ADS) that do not have manually operated driving controls. Those modifications would limit the application of certain requirements for manually operated turn signal, hazard warning signal, and beam switching controls to vehicles with manually operated driving controls. The changes are intended to address regulatory burdens and costs associated with equipment that does not fulfill the same purpose or provide safety benefits in an ADS-equipped vehicle without manually operated driving controls as in a vehicle with such controls. The changes would also narrow certain requirements for telltales to vehicles with manually operated driving controls and incorporate the term \"telltale\" where appropriate throughout the standard. Finally, a proposed addition to the standard would allow cyan-colored ADS marker lamps as optional motor vehicle lighting equipment in ADS-equipped vehicles.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21730","title":"Part 572; Anthropomorphic Test Devices; Test Device for Human Occupant Restraint 50th Percentile Adult Male Dummy (THOR-50M); Extension of Comment Period","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21730/part-572-anthropomorphic-test-devices-test-device-for-human-occupant-restraint-50th-percentile-adult","summary":"In response to a request from the Alliance for Automotive Innovation (Auto Innovators), NHTSA is announcing a 30-day extension of the public comment period for the Supplemental Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (SNPRM) published on September 22, 2026. The SNPRM supplements NHTSA's September 2023 notice of proposed rulemaking to amend NHTSA's regulations to include an advanced crash test dummy (the Test Device for Human Occupant Restraint (THOR) 50th percentile adult male) by requesting comment on specifying an additional spine configuration and an alternative to the face foam, and announcing the availability of additional documents. The comment period for the SNPRM was originally scheduled to end on October 22, 2026. It will now end on November 21, 2026.","publishedAt":"2026-10-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21686","title":"Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes; Correction","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21686/airworthiness-directives-the-boeing-company-airplanes-correction","summary":"The FAA is correcting an airworthiness directive (AD) that was published in the Federal Register. That AD applies to certain The Boeing Company Model 787-8, 787-9, and 787-10 airplanes. As published, a paragraph reference specified in the regulatory text is incorrect. This document corrects that error. In all other respects, the original document remains the same.","publishedAt":"2026-10-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21664","title":"Airworthiness Directives; MD Helicopters, LLC Helicopters","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21664/airworthiness-directives-md-helicopters-llc-helicopters","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain MD Helicopters, LLC (MDHI) Model 369D, 369E, 369F, 369FF, 369H, and 500N helicopters. This AD was prompted by a report of mechanical damage to the main transmission drive shaft coupling (coupling). This AD requires a one-time visual inspection of the couplings for cracks of the splines and, depending on the results, replacement of the couplings. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21647","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities; Renewal of a New Information Collection Request: Request for Revocation of Authority Granted","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21647/agency-information-collection-activities-renewal-of-a-new-information-collection-request-request-for","summary":"In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FMCSA announces its plan to submit the Information Collection Request (ICR) described below to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval. FMCSA requests approval to renew the previously approved ICR now titled \"Request for Revocation of Authority Granted,\" OMB Control No. 2126-0018. This ICR allows certain transportation industry registrants, such as motor carriers, freight forwarders, and property brokers, to request the voluntary revocation of all or part of their operating authority registration utilizing Form OCE-46.","publishedAt":"2026-10-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21642","title":"Request Notice: Use of Foreign-built Small Passenger Vessel in United States Coastwise Trade, M/V LUMINOSITY","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21642/request-notice-use-of-foreign-built-small-passenger-vessel-in-united-states-coastwise-trade-mv","summary":"The Secretary of Transportation, as represented by MARAD, is authorized to make determinations regarding the coastwise use of foreign built; certain U.S. built; and U.S. and foreign rebuilt vessels that solely carry no more than twelve passengers for hire. Information about the requestor's vessel, including a description of the proposed service, is in the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section below.","publishedAt":"2026-10-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21635","title":"Denton County Transportation Authority's Request To Amend Its Positive Train Control Safety Plan and Positive Train Control System","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21635/denton-county-transportation-authoritys-request-to-amend-its-positive-train-control-safety-plan-and","summary":"This document provides the public with notice that, on October 12, 2026, the Denton County Transportation Authority (DCTA) submitted a request for amendment (RFA) to its FRA-approved Positive Train Control Safety Plan (PTCSP) to transition to an integrated dispatch system. The purpose of the transition is to eliminate the need for DCTA dispatch personnel to operate two separate workstations and dispatch systems to perform Centralized Traffic Control (CTC) and Enhanced Automatic Train Control (E-ATC) Temporary Speed Restriction (TSR) operations. As this RFA may involve a request for FRA's approval of proposed material modifications to an FRA-certified positive train control (PTC) system, FRA is publishing this notice and inviting public comment on DCTA's RFA to its PTCSP.","publishedAt":"2026-10-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21590","title":"Airworthiness Directives; General Electric Company Engines","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/22/2026-21590/airworthiness-directives-general-electric-company-engines","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain General Electric Company (GE) Model CF34-8C1, CF34-8C5, CF34- 8C5A1, CF34-8C5A2, CF34-8C5B1, CF34-8E2, CF34-8E2A1, CF34-8E5, CF34- 8E5A1, CF34-8E5A2, CF34-8E5A2HA, CF34-8E6, and CF34-8E6A1 engines. This AD was prompted by reports of in-flight \"Engine Degraded\" messages from the engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS) due to corrosion of the variable geometry (VG) system actuator. This AD requires removing certain electronic engine control (EEC) full authority digital electronic control (FADEC) software versions from service and installing an updated EEC FADEC software that is eligible for installation. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-22","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21565","title":"Establishment of Class E Airspace; Havana, IL","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/22/2026-21565/establishment-of-class-e-airspace-havana-il","summary":"This action establishes Class E airspace at Mason District Hospital Heliport, Havana, IL. This action supports new instrument procedures and instrument flight rule (IFR) operations.","publishedAt":"2026-10-22","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21515","title":"Petition for Waiver of Compliance and Notice of Public Hearing","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/21/2026-21515/petition-for-waiver-of-compliance-and-notice-of-public-hearing","summary":"On July 3, 2025, FRA published notice that Canadian Pacific Kansas City Limited (CPKC) petitioned FRA for relief from certain regulations concerning air brake testing. In this notice, FRA is announcing a public hearing to allow interested persons the opportunity to provide comments on the petition. FRA is also reopening the comment period to allow time for interested parties to submit comments on the petition or in response to views or information provided at the public hearing.","publishedAt":"2026-10-21","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21514","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities; Renewal of an Approved Information Collection: Training Certification for Entry-Level Commercial Motor Vehicle Operators","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/21/2026-21514/agency-information-collection-activities-renewal-of-an-approved-information-collection-training","summary":"In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FMCSA announces its plan to submit the Information Collection Request (ICR) described below to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval and invites public comment. FMCSA requests approval to renew an ICR titled, \"Training Certification for Entry-Level Commercial Motor Vehicle Operators,\" which will continue to be used to register providers of entry-level driver training and to provide State Drivers' Licensing Agencies with information on individuals who have completed said training. If approved, this renewal will allow FMCSA to continue to collect information on registered training providers and entry-level driver training certification information until 2030.","publishedAt":"2026-10-21","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21488","title":"Hours of Service of Drivers: Association of American Railroads and American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association; Application for Exemption Renewal","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/21/2026-21488/hours-of-service-of-drivers-association-of-american-railroads-and-american-short-line-and-regional","summary":"FMCSA announces its final decision to renew and modify the exemption granted to the Association of American Railroads and the American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association and member railroads (the Associations) from the hours-of-service (HOS) prohibitions against driving after the 14th hour after coming on duty (the 14-hour rule) and against driving after accumulating 60 hours of on duty time within 7 consecutive days, or 70 hours of on duty time within 8 consecutive days (the 60-hour/70-hour rule). The exemption will enable covered drivers to respond to unplanned events that occur outside of, or extend beyond, their normal work hours. FMCSA modifies the previous exemption to limit the categories of unplanned events during which the exemption may be used and to add reporting requirements. In addition, only drivers operating for motor carriers listed in the Appendix to this decision may operate under the exemption. FMCSA has analyzed the exemption application and has determined that the exemption renewal, subject to the terms and conditions set forth below, is likely to achieve a level of safety that is equivalent to or greater than the level that would be achieved in the absence of the exemption.","publishedAt":"2026-10-21","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21448","title":"Notice of Petition for Extension of Special Approval","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/20/2026-21448/notice-of-petition-for-extension-of-special-approval","summary":"This document provides the public notice that the Maryland Department of Transportation Maryland Transit Administration MARC Train Service (MACZ), petitioned FRA to extend a special approval of an alternate standard for periodic brake equipment maintenance.","publishedAt":"2026-10-20","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21422","title":"Airspace Designations; Incorporation by Reference Amendment of FAA Order JO 7400.11M","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/20/2026-21422/airspace-designations-incorporation-by-reference-amendment-of-faa-order-jo-740011m","summary":"This action administratively corrects identified final rules published by FAA in the Federal Register between May and September 2026 so that certain published airspace designation amendments are transferred to the most-current revision of FAA Order JO 7400.11, which is incorporated by reference.","publishedAt":"2026-10-20","source":"Federal Register"}]}
